title: Full binary tree: every node has degree 0 or 2
summary: A full binary tree constrains each node’s number of children. It does not require every level to be full.
description: The tree on the left has four levels and 7 unlabeled nodes. The root’s right child is a leaf. Its left child has two children: the left one is a leaf and the right one branches into two more leaves.

A node’s degree is its number of children. The title reads “Full binary tree,” and the gray box says “Every node has 0 or 2 children.” Three internal nodes all have degree 2 and 4 leaves have degree 0. No node has degree 1. The 4 leaves occur on levels two, three, and four.

frames.title: Full binary tree: every node has degree 0 or 2
frames.explanation: A full binary tree requires each node to have 0 or 2 children. Levels may be partially filled and leaves may occur at different levels.
